source.verification: Variable names, question text and Support/Oppose codes for the pre-election grids (CC24_321 to CC24_341) were read from the pre-election questionnaire and the guide. Items marked codesVerified:false come from the guide's label order (post-election wave or non-CC24 names); confirm the numeric codes and per-row variable names against the CSV header before use. The post questionnaire was not read.

items.question: Repeal the Affordable Care Act
Prevent the government from banning gas stove
Renew the federal surveillance programs ... without a search warrant
items.notes: Oppose = less government reach.

items.question: Spend $150 billion a year for 8 years on construction and repair of roads and bridges, rail...
items.notes: Also loads on fiscal-restraint and collective-provision.

items.question: Give the Environmental Protection Agency power to regulate carbon dioxide emissions
items.notes: Cross-loads with environmental-stewardship; treat as secondary.

items.question: Expand Medicaid to cover individuals making less than $25,000 and families making less than $40,000 a year.
Spend $150 billion a year for 8 years on construction and repair of roads and bridges, rail...
State legislature spending -- Welfare / Health Care / Education / Transportation-Infrastructure (rows of one grid)
items.notes: Post-election wave (asked of about 49,000). Rows are welfare, health care, education, law enforcement, transportation/infrastructure; per-row variable suffix not confirmed in the guide. Increase = more.

items.question: Expand federal tax incentives to encourage developers to build homes for people who make less than half of the average income
Forgive up to $20,000 of student loan debt for each person
items.notes: The codebook questionnaire names this row CC24_323f inside the CC24_328 grid (apparent typo in the questionnaire). Which name the CSV uses is unverified; check both.

items.question: Relax local zoning laws in your state to allow for construction of more apartments and condos.
items.notes: Weak: wording does not say who overrides local rules. Oppose read as keeping local land-use authority.

items.question: Supreme Court decisions -- ... individual states can make their own laws governing abortion
items.notes: Weak: the Dobbs row is about states, not local bodies. Row suffix unconfirmed.

items.question: How much trust do you have in the government of the state where you live ...
items.notes: Weak proxy: use trust in state minus trust in federal (CC24_423). Higher relative trust in the lower level = more local control.

items.question: State legislature spending (welfare, health care, education, law enforcement, transportation rows)
items.notes: Decrease = more restraint. Averaged across rows.

items.question: Spend $150 billion a year for 8 years on construction and repair of roads and bridges, rail...
Forgive up to $20,000 of student loan debt for each person
items.notes: Questionnaire names this row CC24_323f; see collective-provision note.

items.question: Expand Medicaid to cover individuals making less than $25,000 ...
Extend the tax cuts enacted in 2017 ...
items.notes: Weak: raising revenue helps balance a budget; a deficit-minded reading. Secondary only.

items.question: Supreme Court decisions -- The use of race in university admissions violates Equal Protection ...
items.notes: Reads equal treatment as race-blind rules. Conflicts with equal-opportunity reading, so direction depends on the game's definition. Row suffix unconfirmed.

items.question: Require that all federal agencies recognize same-sex marriages and interracial marriages.
Racial Resentment rows, e.g. 'Whites get away with offenses that African Americans would never get away with.'
items.notes: Agree = sees unequal treatment; this is perceived unequal treatment, not support for equal rules. Weak.

items.question: Always allow a woman the right to obtain an abortion as a matter of choice
Prohibit government restrictions on the provision of, and access to, contraceptives.
Prohibit government restrictions on the provision of, and access to, abortion services.
Make it easier for people to obtain concealed-carry permit

items.question: State policies (gender transition surgery for minors; parental consent for pronouns; abortion pills by mail; travel for abortion; age verification)
items.notes: Oppose = more liberty for rows on bans; mixed for parental consent. Rows share the CC24_444 stem; suffixes unconfirmed.

Require criminal background checks on all gun sales
Ban assault rifles

Increase spending on mental health and school safety; Allow police to confiscate guns from people deemed to be dangerous by a judge; ...

items.question: State legislature spending -- Law Enforcement

items.question: Relax local zoning laws in your state to allow for construction of more apartments and condos.

items.question: Halt new oil and gas leases on federal lands

items.question: Give the Environmental Protection Agency power to regulate carbon dioxide emissions
Require that at least 20 percent of electricity be generated with renewable sources such as wind, solar, or hydroelectric power
Strengthen the Environmental Protection Agency enforcement of the Clean Air Act and Clean Water Act even if it costs U.S. jobs
Increase fossil fuel production in the U.S.

Expand federal tax incentives to encourage developers to build homes for people who make less than half of the average income
Provide permanent resident status to children of immigrants who were brought to the United States by their parents (also known as Dreamers)...
White people in the U.S. have certain advantages because of the color of their skin.
items.notes: Agree = sees unequal starting points. Rows of one grid; suffix unconfirmed.

items.question: Generations of slavery and discrimination have created conditions that make it difficult for Blacks to work their way out of the lower class.
items.notes: Agree = starting place limits where one can get. Row suffix unconfirmed.

items.question: Relax local zoning laws in your state to allow for construction of more apartments and condos.
items.notes: Housing access; secondary.

items.question: How important is religion in your life?
items.notes: Weak proxy for traditionalism, not for support of old arrangements.

items.question: Aside from weddings and funerals, how often do you attend religious services?
items.notes: Weak proxy. Codes assumed from label order (1 = more than once a week ... 6 = never, 8 = don't know in the guide's listing).

items.question: Require that all federal agencies recognize same-sex marriages and interracial marriages.
items.notes: Weak proxy: oppose = favors older marriage norms.

items.question: Women seek to gain power by getting control over men. / Women are too easily offended.
items.notes: Weak proxy for traditional gender attitudes; agree = more.

items.question: Elections in the U.S. are fair / Your state or local government conducted a fair and accurate election in 2024
items.notes: Very weak: measures trust in process, not demand for openness. Disagree used only as a proxy for wanting more scrutiny.

items.question: How much trust do you have in the federal government in Washington ...
items.notes: Very weak: low trust may drive demand for openness.

items.question: Require able-bodied adults under 64 years of age who do not have dependents to have a job in order to receive Medicaid.
items.notes: Very weak proxy: oppose = favors protecting low-wage people from conditions. No minimum wage, union or labor item found in the 2024 guide.

items.question: Strengthen the Environmental Protection Agency enforcement ... even if it costs U.S. jobs
items.notes: Very weak: trades jobs against rules. Reverse of worker protection only loosely.

items.question: State policies -- School voucher subsidies for families to send their children to private or charter schools
items.notes: Weak proxy: school choice. Row suffix unconfirmed.

items.question: Raise the corporate income tax rate from 21 percent to 28 percent
items.notes: Weak proxy: lower business taxes.

items.question: Allow tax rates on those earning $400,000 or more a year to rise to 35 percent
items.notes: Weak proxy.

items.question: Increase fossil fuel production in the U.S.
items.notes: Weak proxy: production, not competition.

notes: Pre-election grid rows are named CC24_321a-f, CC24_323a-d, CC24_324a-d, CC24_326a-f, CC24_328a-e (plus a row the questionnaire calls CC24_323f), CC24_340a-f, CC24_341a-d. Each has Support=1, Oppose=2, 8=Skipped, 9=Not Asked.
Post-election items CC24_420 to CC24_445 appear in the guide only as grids or stems; per-row variable names (for example CC24_443_1 or CC24_443a) are not confirmed.

Immigration items CC24_323a-d and CC24_340f, and CC24_325 (abortion weeks), CC24_324b-d, are not mapped to any value because none fits cleanly. CC24_323b/c and CC24_340f (deny asylum) could be a weak public-safety proxy (support = more).
The 2024 guide has no trade, tariff, minimum wage, union or voter ID item in the common content. Transparency and worker-protection have no real CES measure.
CC24_330a (self-rated ideology, 1 Very Liberal to 7 Very Conservative) is available as a general anchor but maps to no single value.
Several items load on two values (CC24_341d, CC24_328a, CC24_340e, CC24_326e); the game should pick one primary value per use or split weights.
